object.definition: The complete data and row order of an arbitrary real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ are fixed in advance. Each n-dimensional row arrives once.

assumption.description: Fixed input order; the entire data sequence is chosen before play begins.

norm.definition: Euclidean vector norm $\|z\|_2=(\sum_i|z_i|^2)^{1/2}$ and matrix operator norm $\|M\|_{\rm op}=\max_{\|z\|_2=1}\|Mz\|_2$; define $\|M\|_F=(\sum_{ij}|M_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$.

bindings.source_value: Randomized single-pass streaming algorithms are permitted. State consists of exact-real registers updated by ordinary arithmetic and comparisons. Uncharged arbitrary encodings that compress the entire real input stream into one register are excluded. Apart from the single-pass and register-memory constraints, internal arithmetic time is unrestricted.

bindings.source_value: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.

The algorithm is selected using only public inputs. For every admissible input fixed before its private seed is generated, the success event has probability at least $2/3$ over that private randomness.

protocols.adversary_information: oblivious fixed input; does not see private seed
protocols.loss_bearing_points: Evaluate the full-matrix projection error only at termination. There is no roundwise online regret.
steps: The input provider fixes the complete matrix A and row order before the private seed is drawn.
Reveal the rows of A sequentially. The algorithm updates its state after reading each row.
Previous input rows are discarded and cannot be requested again.
Final output is an encoding of a rank-$k$ subspace.
